profiles.meeting_scenario: Helix Metrics, a business-intelligence company serving universities and research funders, is planning a 10-week pilot for a new evaluation product inspired by Scientific Research Measures (SRM). The product will let institutions compare researchers using a calibrated, field-sensitive score built from a scholar's full citation profile rather than a single bibliometric index. In this planning meeting, the team needs to align on what will be included in the pilot, how the calibration step will be done, what materials will be shown to the client, and what counts as being ready for the pilot kickoff with a flagship university customer. The agenda is to define the pilot package, assign responsibilities for methodology and client-facing assets, and confirm the timeline for a late-May kickoff. The expected outcome is an agreed plan for deliverables, owners, and sequencing that both participants believe supports the same pilot launch.

members.name: Lena Ortiz
members.expertise: Research analytics products, enterprise pilots, university procurement cycles
members.background: Lena previously managed product rollouts for academic benchmarking tools and now leads commercial planning for new analytics offerings at Helix Metrics.
members.private_state: She wants the pilot scoped tightly enough to be demoable within the quarter and to generate a renewal path without triggering a long methodology review by the client.
hidden_assumptions: "Community calibration" means setting discipline-level baselines once for the pilot using broad field norms that can later be reused across customers.
"Whole citation record" for a commercial pilot means the publications already covered in the firm's standard indexed-data feed, not edge-case outputs that require manual curation.
"Pilot-ready" means the client can see stable-looking scores, sample dashboards, and a clear narrative, even if governance details like appeals or audit logs are added after kickoff.
If they say the kickoff is in late May, work due that week can land by end of day in the client's local timezone and still be considered on time.

members.name: Dr. Marcus Feld
members.expertise: Bibliometrics, quantitative evaluation models, calibration of field-normalized indicators
members.background: Marcus is a former scientometrics researcher who joined Helix Metrics to translate academic measurement frameworks into defensible institutional products.
members.private_state: He wants the pilot to preserve methodological credibility so it can later be published as a case study and withstand scrutiny from faculty committees.
hidden_assumptions: "Community calibration" means tailoring the scoring function to the specific scholarly community being evaluated, using direct input from that community before scores are shown.
"Whole citation record" includes all scholarly outputs materially relevant in the field, including books, book chapters, and manually linked records where indexed coverage is weak.
"Pilot-ready" means scores are externally defensible: documented methodology, traceable source records, and a basic review path for contested profiles.
A late-May kickoff implies materials must be finalized early enough for internal academic review before the client meeting, effectively several days earlier than the meeting date itself.

misalignment_points.surface_form: "We'll calibrate the SRM to the community before kickoff."
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means Helix will apply prebuilt discipline-level calibration curves for broad fields such as economics, biomedicine, and engineering so the pilot can launch quickly.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means Helix will calibrate specifically to the client's scholarly community, using input from local faculty or a designated expert panel before any scores are presented.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase comes directly from the product concept and sounds shared and precise, but both treat the word "community" as obviously referring to the relevant audience in their own way, so neither thinks to unpack whether it means a field at large or the client's local academic cohort.

misalignment_points.topic: Boundary of the whole citation record
misalignment_points.surface_form: "We'll use the whole citation record for the pilot profiles."
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this includes every publication already present in Helix's normal indexed sources for each faculty member, which mostly covers journal articles and major conference proceedings.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes this extends to all significant scholarly outputs in the department, including books, chapters, and manually reconciled records that are important in unevenly indexed areas.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both believe they are endorsing the same high-level principle of being more inclusive than legacy metrics; because nobody lists publication types one by one, the hidden difference in data boundaries remains invisible.

misalignment_points.surface_form: "Let's make sure the scorecard is pilot-ready by late May."
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks pilot-ready means the score outputs are stable enough for client demos, dashboard screenshots, and a persuasive explanation of benefits.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks pilot-ready means the score outputs are auditable and reviewable, with method notes, profile traceability, and a lightweight challenge process for disputed records.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both naturally use the same project-management phrase and assume the other shares the standard of readiness appropriate to a pilot, but each silently imports standards from their own function: sales enablement for M1 and methodological defensibility for M2.

misalignment_points.surface_form: "We can get community input in parallel while data prep is running."
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this means sending a short asynchronous questionnaire to a few external advisors and using existing benchmark preferences already collected by the commercial team.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes this means convening a structured review session with the client's senior faculty panel to discuss field norms and edge cases before parameter settings are finalized.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: They agree on the same objective and timing language, so the difference in execution method hides beneath the word "input"; each method seems like a routine implementation detail rather than something requiring explicit negotiation.

turns.inner_thought: I need this pilot boxed tightly enough that we can show Northbridge something polished within the quarter and keep them moving toward renewal. The big risk is letting methodology expand into a review exercise before kickoff. For me, pilot-ready by late May means stable-looking scores, some clean comparison views, and a client story that lands well in the meeting. We can layer governance mechanics later if the pilot sticks.

turns.inner_thought: Good. If we do this, it has to demonstrate that SRM is not just another normalized index with a new label. The credibility hinge is calibration. When I say calibrate the SRM to the community before kickoff, I mean we need actual input from the scholarly community being assessed so the scoring function is defensible later with faculty committees and potentially publishable as a case study.

turns.inner_thought: We should keep data assembly inside the normal indexed-data feed. That's the fastest route and already supports most faculty profiles well enough for a pilot. When I say whole citation record, I mean everything already in our standard coverage for those faculty members; I do not want this turning into a manual hunt for hard-to-index outputs.
